# C6 — Spring margin consistency

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **SUPPORTED WITHIN STATED LIMITS** — Evidence supports the statement as worded, at its evidence class only. |
| Strongest accepted evidence | MODEL ONLY |
| Evidence classes cited | IMPLEMENTATION, TEST PROCEDURE, ANALYTICAL |
| Gate reached | SOFTWARE REPRODUCTION (next: SYNTHETIC TEST) |
| Last review | CURRENT — human recorded 2026-11-14 by chief weapons engineer |

**Question.** Does the specified torsion spring exceed the calculated minimum rate by at least 20 percent at the shared design point?

**Current statement.** At the Phase 1 militarized design point the spring drives the four-bar crank. The binding requirement is the lock: at the deployed stop the preload torque must exceed the fin hold moment reflected through the worst-case back-drive ratio. That gives k_min = 7.82 N*m/rad (the deployment-energy requirement gives only 2.13). The specified 11.0 N*m/rad spring gives a 40.6 percent margin, above the 20 percent requirement. No spring has been characterized; the rate is a specified catalog-scale value.

- [D-012](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-012) (RESOLVED) Test named for a 20% margin did not enforce it

## Assumptions

- The requirement and the reported margin use the same definition: (k_supplied - k_min) / k_min.
- The hold case is max flight dynamic pressure with a 15 deg gust angle of attack and a 1.4x tolerance growth of the back-drive ratio.

## Limitations

- The hold-moment and friction values are modeled, not measured.
- The spring rate is specified, not characterized.
- The legacy fin-direct record (schema /1, 19.0 percent margin at the historical design point) is kept for traceability.

## Measurement needed to close the next gate

- Inert torque-angle characterization of the supplied spring (proposed pre-registration P-002).
- Friction measurement of a built hinge.

## Pre-registered experiments

- P-002 (proposed)

- Any inert physical measurement: none has been accepted for this claim.
- Physical performance of any hardware.
- Flight readiness or safety for live propulsion.
